title: Watchtower: Reliability Launch Playbook — cross-functional activation plan
content:
Purpose
This is a tactical launch playbook for the Watchtower reliability program — a coordinated, cross-functional effort to set service-level objectives (SLOs), establish guardrails for error budgets, and run the first org-wide SLO rollout across model-serving and control-plane surfaces.

Audience
- SRE/Platform leads
- Product & Feature owners for model serving (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
- Engineering managers (Serving runtime, Platform, Observability)
- Solutions & Customer Success stakeholders for customer impact modeling

Context and constraints
- Why now: increased adoption of Dedicated and Private has created variability in tail latency and regional availability; exec priority to demonstrate measurable uptime guarantees by end of Q2.
- Constraint: metrics pipeline (ingest/aggregation) currently supports 1s token-level metrics for hosted but needs stable retention/rollups for private deployments (work in REL-901).
- Risk: rollout during major product launch windows (see product calendar) — mitigate with canary and progressive windows.

High-level goals (OKRs for this initiative)
- Launch SLOs and dashboards for top 6 model-serving routes with automated error-budget tracking (Objective)
  - KR1: 99.5% availability P99 within 30d for API route /v1/generate
  - KR2: Error budget alerts configured and tested for 3 severity levels
  - KR3: 90-day retention of SLI histograms for postmortem analysis

Scope (what’s in / out)
- In: API surface (text generation, chat), core inference runtime metrics (latency, error-rate), token pipeline SLIs, runbooks for oncall
- Out: embeddings-only offline pipelines, billing analytics (handled separately)

Key definitions (team alignment)
- SLI (service-level indicator): request-level success (HTTP 2xx) and tail latency (P99 request latency measured at gateway)
- SLO (objective): rolling 30d P99 latency and rolling 30d availability target per route
- Error budget policy: consume budget based on 30d window; automatic throttling of non-critical experimental routes at 50% consumption

Stakeholders & RACI snapshot
- Program lead (R): Maya Patel (SRE)
- Metrics/observability (A): Ethan Chen (obs lead)
- Runtime instrumentation (C): Priya Rao (serving-runtime)
- Product owner (C): Sofia Alvarez (product-hosted-api)
- Release & rollout (I): Platform eng, Solutions eng, Customer Success
- Exec sponsor (I): Jonas Becker (VP SRE)

Milestones & timeline (quarter view)
- Week 0 (kickoff): alignment workshop — owners, SLIs, target windows (complete 2027-02-14)
- Week 2: instrumentation gaps triage & tasks (REL-780), ingest pipeline ETA for rollups (OBS-221)
- Week 4: dashboards + synthetic tests live for top-6 routes; first canary (10% traffic)
- Week 6: error budget automation + alerting (pager + slack) wired; runbook drafts published
- Week 8: progressive rollout to 50% traffic; internal retro & gating review
- Week 12: full rollout and post-launch 30d monitoring window begins

Deliverables (owner and acceptance criteria)
- SLO spec doc (Maya) — includes precise SLI formulas, measurement windows, and aggregation method; accepted when reviewed & signed by Product and Obs (Linear REL-1234)
- Instrumentation backlog (Priya) — list of missing spans/metrics with PRs; acceptance: merged PRs + test coverage
- Dashboards & synthetic tests (Ethan) — for each SLO route: SLI trend, error-budget burn rate, canary view; acceptance: automated synthetic failing test triggers alert
- Runbooks (oncall playbooks) (SRE squad leads) — steps for mitigation and rollback; acceptance: tabletop drill passes in 2/3 scenarios
- Communications play (Sofia) — customer-facing FAQ, internal comms template; acceptance: reviewed by Legal & CS

Instrumentation & metrics details (practical)
- Primary SLI: request_success = count(HTTP_status in 200..299) / count(total requests) sampled at edge LB aggregated to 1m buckets, then rolled to 5m and 30d windows for SLO eval
- Latency SLI: p99_request_latency computed from end-to-end request timing at API gateway plus dequeue time; exclude synthetic & healthcheck routes
- Tagging: route_name, model_variant, region, customer_tier (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Backfill plan: for private deployments missing 30d historical rollups, compute warm-up SLOs using 7d with explicit note in dashboard

Canary & rollout playbook (minimal-disturbance)
- Canary phases: 0% -> 10% (1d) -> 25% (3d) -> 50% (5d) -> 100% (gated)
- Gates: error-budget burn > 5%/24h OR sustained P99 degradation > 15% from baseline triggers freeze and rollback to previous model-variant or route config
- Fallback actions: automatic traffic steering to 'degraded' model variant with reduced context-length (prebuilt compatible variant), and enable token-cache bypass if cache corruption suspected

Oncall & staffing impacts
- Temporary SLO rotation: create a Watchtower oncall roster for 8 weeks comprised of SRE shifts + rotated serving-runtime engineers; schedule in PagerDuty tag 'watchtower-rollout'
- Training: 1hr tabletop + 30m demo for runbook changes, mandatory for oncall & platform leads before Week 4

Communications plan
- Internal: weekly status digest (owner: Maya) + Slack channel #watchtower-launch for real-time ops notes. Use short-form updates in Exec readout twice in the quarter.
- External: Customer Success will own a notification template to customers in impacted tiers for major rollouts; for enterprise Dedicated customers, Solutions will run dedicated tech-check calls

Decision log (open questions)
- Q1: Should SLO windows be 7d + 30d aggregated or 30d rolling only? (Tradeoffs: sensitivity v. stability) — Action: decide by 2027-02-18 (Maya + Product)
- Q2: Default SLO targets per route for Private deployments where control plane is not visible — fallback to routing-level SLOs or require agent instrumentation? (Priya to propose) due 2027-02-22
- Q3: Postmortem policy when error budget exhausted for customer-facing routes — auto-sla credits? (Finance & Legal consult)

Risk matrix (top 5)
- Missing durable metrics for private deployments -> Mitigation: temporary narrower SLO window, customer opt-in instrumentation
- False positives from synthetic tests -> Mitigation: multi-synthetic confirmation + threshold smoothing
- Oncall fatigue during rollouts -> Mitigation: additional paid rotation + automated remediation playbooks
- Canary rollouts impact latency spikes -> Mitigation: traffic shaping and immediate rollback circuits
- Cross-team dependency delays (observability, runtime) -> Mitigation: execute parallel workstreams, weekly unblocker meeting

Runbook checklist (quick start)
- Confirm alert routing -> PagerDuty escalation path exists
- Verify synthetic test failure triggers -> Slack + PagerDuty hooks validated
- Ensure rollback artifacts present -> previous model variant pinned and tested in staging
- Publish customer comms draft -> CS & Legal sign-off

Meeting cadence & rituals
- Kickoff: alignment workshop (Week 0)
- Weekly: Watchtower status sync (30m) — owners report blocked items, burn rate, instrumentation progress
- Twice-weekly: Observability & Runtime standup (15m) during canary weeks
- Postmortem retro: 1 week after each major rollout gate decision

Acceptance & success criteria (how we know rollout worked)
- All top-6 routes reporting SLOs with < 5% error-budget burn over the first 30d after full rollout
- At least two runbook tabletop drills completed with documented improvements
- No more than one production rollback that required manual failover across the rollout period

Next steps (immediate)
- Maya: run SLO alignment workshop — complete by 2027-02-14
- Priya: open instrumentation epic with first 5PRs for gateway timing by 2027-02-18 (REL-780)
- Ethan: seed dashboards and synthetic tests in staging by 2027-02-21 (OBS-221)
- Sofia: draft customer comms and internal FAQ by 2027-02-25

Notes to self / rough brainstorms (working-area fragments)
- Think about adding a "degraded-tier" traffic class for experiments — gives a controlled path for lower-priority traffic during high burn
- Could we use KV-cache metrics as an early proxy for tail latency regressions? (Priya to research)
- Long-term: compute cost-to-serve per SLO bucket to feed Optimize recommendations

Appendix: quick links and tickets
- Confluence: Watchtower program overview (link above)
- Linear: REL-1234 (SLO spec), REL-780 (instrumentation), OBS-221 (dashboard/synthetic)
- GitHub: PRs for gateway timing and tagging (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/482)

Document history
- 2027-02-10: initial draft (Maya)
- 2027-02-14: alignment workshop notes added
- 2027-02-18: instrumentation tasking and dates updated (Ethan, Priya)
